The ASOW has a periodic serpentine structure with broken longitudinal symmetry, achieved by having different phase accumulation in the left and right segments of the unit cell.
The authors derive a 6x6 transfer matrix formalism to model the electromagnetic fields in the ASOW and obtain the Bloch eigenmodes.
An SIP is defined as a third-order exceptional point of degeneracy, where three Bloch eigenmodes with the same sign of the real part of the wavenumber coalesce.
The authors provide a set of five necessary conditions in Eq. (14) that must be satisfied for the ASOW to exhibit an SIP.
The finite-length ASOW supporting an SIP shows a frozen mode regime with dramatically enhanced field amplitudes in the middle of the structure compared to the edges.
The transfer function of the finite-length ASOW reaches a maximum near the SIP frequency, while the reflection function is minimized.
The quality factor (Q) is high in the vicinity of the SIP due to the frozen mode regime, but does not reach extremely high values as the SIP is not a cavity resonance.
The ASOW can support both SIPs and regular band edges (RBEs) in a small frequency range, which could be problematic for applications like lasers.
The authors use a coalescence parameter σ to quantify the degree of coalescence of the Bloch eigenmodes at the SIP.
The ASOW is modeled using a silicon-on-insulator waveguide structure with a height of 230 nm and a width of 430 nm, operating at a wavelength of 1550 nm.
The authors consider ASOW loops with a radius R ≥ 10 μm to minimize radiation losses at optical frequencies.
The transfer matrix of the ASOW unit cell satisfies det(T_u) = 1 due to the reciprocity of the structure.
The dispersion diagram of the ASOW is symmetric with respect to the center of the Brillouin zone due to the reciprocity of the structure.
The authors calculate the field amplitudes along the finite-length ASOW by applying the boundary conditions at the input and output.
The distance between peaks in the transfer and reflection functions decreases as the number of unit cells N increases.
